### Loading libraries

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```

### Loading the data

Uses the one created in the end of the 03_augment file

```{r}
load(here("data", "03_cancer_augment.RData"))
```

```{r}
clinical_augment
```

#### Boxplot of the survival for each type of cancer

To give an overview of the different cancer types.

```{r}
g1 <- ggplot(data = clinical_augment,
            mapping = aes(y = cancer_type,
                          x = os_months)) + 
  geom_boxplot()+
  labs(title = 'Survival for each cancer type',
       x = 'Time (Months)',
       y = 'Cancer type')
g1
```

Col-plot of the survival chance for each cancer type, grouped by sex.

```{r}
survival_percentage <- clinical_augment |> 
  group_by(cancer_type, sex) |> 
  summarise(number_of_patients = n(),
  average_survival = mean(os_months, na.rm = TRUE),
  alive = sum(status == 'LIVING', na.rm = TRUE),
  survival_percent = alive / number_of_patients * 100,
  .groups = 'drop')

g2 <- ggplot(data = survival_percentage,
             mapping = aes(x = cancer_type,
                           y = survival_percent,
                           fill = sex)) + 
  geom_col(position = 'dodge')+
  labs (title = 'Survival percentage for each cancer type',
        x = 'Cancer type',
        y = 'Survival percent (%)')+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(
    angle = 20,
    hjust = 0.75))
g2
```

This show that the cancer with the lowest survival rate is glioma, followed by breast cancer.\
The highest chance of survival is for Skin-cancer, non-melanoma (this is only for 1 patient how survived, so is not a good sample size for this kind).\
Disregarding the odd one, the one of the collectively highest survival percentage is the melanoma.

```{r}
survival_percentage <- clinical_augment |> 
  group_by(sex) |> 
  summarise(
    number_of_patients = n(),
    alive = sum(status == 'LIVING', na.rm = TRUE),
    survival_percent = alive / number_of_patients * 100)
g3 <- ggplot(data = survival_percentage,
             mapping = aes(x = sex,
                           y = survival_percent,
                           fill = sex)) + 
  geom_col(position = 'dodge')+
  labs (title = 'Survival percentage for each cancer type',
        x = 'Sex',
        y = 'Survival percent (%)')+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(
    angle = 20,
    hjust = 0.75))
g3
```

```{r}
survival_curve_test <- clinical_augment |> 
  group_by(cancer_type,os_months) |> 
  summarise(
    deaths = sum(status == 'DECEASED'),
    living = sum(status == 'LIVING'),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) |> 
  
  arrange(cancer_type,os_months) |> 
  
  group_by(cancer_type) |> 
  mutate(
    at_risk = rev(cumsum(rev(deaths + living))),
    survival = cumprod(1 - deaths/at_risk)
  ) |> 
  ungroup()


#survival_curve_test
g1 <- ggplot(data = survival_curve_test,
             
             mapping = aes(x = os_months,
                           y = survival,
                           color = cancer_type))+
  geom_step()+
  labs(title = 'Overall survival by cancer type',
       x = 'Overall survival (months)',
       y = 'Survival probability',
       color = 'Cancer types')+
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = 'bottom')+
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      title.position ='top'))
g1
```

This is survival probability over time for each cancer types. Showing that the type have a big impact in length and probability of survival.

```{r}


#survival_curve_test
g1 <- ggplot(data = survival_curve_test |> 
             filter(cancer_type %in% c('Melanoma','Glioma')),
             mapping = aes(x = os_months,
                           y = survival,
                           color = cancer_type))+
  geom_step()+
  labs(title = 'Overall survival by cancer type',
       x = 'Overall survival (months)',
       y = 'Survival probability',
       color = 'Cancer types')+
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = 'bottom')
g1
```

To look more closely on two quite different, we have chosen glioma, one of the lowest survival percentage, and melanoma, one of the highest survival percentage.

Here it is more clear, that the type of cancer impacts survival a lot.

In the melanoma case, some stayed and survived all the way, while with glioma the people surviving the cancer where done with the follow-up earlier than for melanoma(?)
